Sparse Volume Data Structures (SVDS) is a family of hybrid volume data structures that decompose a 3D volume into bricks, assigning each brick one of several "elemental node types" (empty, voxel list, pointer octree, or dense) based on local sparsity to minimize memory consumption [S1, unofficial].

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S1]. The source explicitly defines a hybrid data structure composed of four 'elemental node types': Empty, Voxel list, Octree (specifically pointer octree), and Dense volume. It states that these structures are used to represent bricks of a volume and that the system optimizes memory by locally adapting these node types based on sparsity (e.g., using empty bricks for omitted data, voxel lists for extremely sparse data, and dense grids for very dense data). The specific details regarding memory efficiency, access times, and structural properties mentioned in the claim are consistent with the provided notes and passages.
